input_summary: Autoimmune case review: suspected SLE with fever, malar rash, oral ulcers, proteinuria, anti-dsDNA positive; considering prednisone; assess infection safety risk and evidence convergence.
answer_preview: The case strongly supports systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) given the presence of malar rash, oral ulcers, proteinuria, fever, and positive anti-dsDNA. Evidence from clinical literature (obs_0001) and mechanism evidence (obs_0002) corroborate SLE pathogenesis. Regarding prednisone safety, drug safety signals (obs_0003) indicate infection risks including pneumonia and tuberculosis, which should be considered but do not preclude use with appropriate monitoring. Evidence convergence is sufficient
